title: Chapter 19
content:
Gasping and groaning, Jakyeong sat bolt upright in bed.

Cold sweat beaded thickly across his forehead, drenching the collar of his shirt. For several disoriented seconds, he scanned the room, unable to separate the nightmare from reality.

It had been a visceral, suffocating horror. Kang Il-hyun had cornered him, shot him dead-center, and methodically sliced off each of Jakyeong's fingers with a blade before popping them into his own mouth like cocktail sausages.

The phantom memory was so vivid Jakyeong could almost feel the severed flesh resting on his tongue. He ran his teeth over his gums, confirmed his mouth was empty, and collapsed back onto the pillows with a ragged breath.

He rarely dreamed, but yesterday's sheer psychological warfare had clearly taken a toll.

He tried closing his eyes, but sleep was gone. Checking his watch, he realized the morning was already half-spent. At times like this, sweating it out in a gym would work wonders. Maybe he should take a run around the perimeter? He walked to the floor-to-ceiling windows and drew back the blinds. The sun was already riding high in the sky.

The sharp whine of a power drill echoed from the courtyard below. The construction crew was putting the finishing touches on the outdoor swimming pool. With matching cabana umbrellas, teak patio tables, and reclining sun loungers set up along the stone deck, the estate had taken on the sleek, luxurious ambiance of a high-end resort.

Jakyeong threw on his clothes and headed downstairs.

In the living room, Kang Il-hyun sat lounging on the sofa, casually leafing through the morning paper.

"Good morning, Director Kang," Jakyeong called out, deliberately pitching his tone light and cheerful.

Il-hyun lowered the newspaper, his eyes drifting over Jakyeong. "Did you sleep well? You look radiant this morning. Must have had quite a peaceful night."

Jakyeong forced a thin, bitter smile. The nightmare of getting his fingers eaten flashed behind his eyes. They say dreams are the opposite of reality, right? He clung to the superstition for comfort.

Stepping into the kitchen, he exchanged warm greetings with the housekeeper, brewed a fresh mug of black coffee, and returned to the main hall.

Il-hyun had moved to the glass wall, standing tall as he looked out over the grounds.

Beyond the pool construction, an unfamiliar dog was trotting alongside a security handler. It was a massive German Shepherd—broad-chested, muscular, and carrying a distinctly vicious edge.

"You have a dog..." Jakyeong murmured, stepping beside him.

"He's been mine for years," Il-hyun replied smoothly. "Just returned from the behavioral camp."

"A camp? Why was he sent away?"

"He mauled a man to death."

Jakyeong glanced over, catching the utter indifference in Il-hyun’s profile.

"Granted, the target was a dead man anyway," Il-hyun added, "but even attack dogs require discipline."

"Ah..."

Il-hyun turned, his dark eyes curving into an amused, charming smile. "Whether it's an animal or a human, I believe in granting at least one second chance."

Jakyeong nodded along, mirroring the smile until his cheek muscles twitched from the strain. Staring at this man after waking from a nightmare about him was making his nervous system short-circuit. It was past 10:00 AM—why hadn't the bastard left for the office yet? He usually disappeared at the crack of dawn, but today he was taking his sweet time.

"The pool is enormous," Jakyeong said, desperate to change the subject. It wasn't a lie; the basin was olympic-tier.

"They tell me it'll be fully operational by this afternoon. I'm looking forward to it."

"You enjoy swimming?"

"I excel at all athletics," Il-hyun stated with effortless arrogance. "How about you, Yi-an?"

I asked if you enjoyed it, not if you were an Olympic medalist, you smug prick.

"I enjoy swimming as well," Jakyeong replied with meek modesty.

"Splendid. We'll have to take a swim together before you return to Hong Kong."

Jakyeong gave an awkward, sheepish nod, internally recoiling at the thought. The last thing he wanted was to strip down and splash around with a lethal hitman. As he plotted a graceful retreat to the second floor, his peripheral vision caught something in the dense tree line beyond the manicured lawn.

A faint, metallic glint flickered between the leaves.

What was that...?

He thought his eyes were playing tricks on him, but instinct took over before logic could catch up.

His body moved on pure muscle memory.

Jakyeong lunged, slamming his entire weight into Kang Il-hyun. Before their bodies even crashed onto the hardwood floor, a deafening CRACK shattered the air as high-velocity rounds punched through the heavy glass panel, obliterating the priceless oil painting hanging directly behind them into a shower of canvas and plaster.

THUD!

Il-hyun hit the floor with Jakyeong pinned flat on top of him.

Before either could register the impact, a second sniper round tore through the frame. The sheer explosion of noise sent the domestic staff screaming from the kitchen.

"Get back inside! Down!" Jakyeong roared at the top of his lungs.

Outside, the German Shepherd was barking maniacally, drowned out by the frantic shouts of armed guards scrambling into formation.

Panting heavily, Jakyeong held his position, every sense tuned to the tree line. No third round followed. The estate fell into a breathless, suffocating silence.

The man beneath him was the first to speak.

"Mind getting off me...?"

Still scanning the perimeter, Jakyeong looked down at the face trapped beneath his chest.

"Having you straddle me and pant like that... is driving me insane."

Il-hyun’s tone was completely level, oozing leisurely amusement. Worse, Jakyeong could feel something unmistakably rigid and growing between his thighs.

Jakyeong scrambled off him in sheer, unadulterated horror.

What the actual fuck?! In the middle of an assassination attempt?!

Jakyeong stared at him with venomous revulsion, but Il-hyun merely flashed an unbothered, slick grin as he pushed himself up.

Right on cue, several security guards burst into the living room, with Park Tae-soo leading the charge.

"Are you unharmed, Executive Director?!"

Il-hyun stood up, casually brushing off his dress shirt as he strode right up to the shattered window. Tae-soo rushed forward, throwing his arms out to shield him.

"Sir, stay back! It's too dangerous, you need to take cover—"

Il-hyun stared through the gaping bullet hole in the glass, his brows drawing together in a furious, terrifying scowl.

"Track him down and drag him here."

"Our perimeter teams are already in pursuit, sir—"

Il-hyun snapped his head around, his eyes locking onto Tae-soo with arctic malice. "Not the shooter. The contractor who installed this glass."

Tae-soo froze mid-breath. Jakyeong stared, utterly dumbfounded.

"Fucking scammers..." Il-hyun gritted his teeth, his voice dropping into a lethal growl. "Charged me a fortune for military-grade ballistic plating, and it punches through like cardboard."

"..."

"Actually, scratch that. Don't drag him here—just bury the bastard alive. Make sure he never sees the sun again."

"Understood, sir," Tae-soo bowed instantly.

Il-hyun’s gaze slowly drifted over, locking onto Jakyeong.

The weight of that stare was suffocating. Shit. Flirting his way out of last night's mess was one thing, but reacting to a sniper's optic glint and tackling a syndicate boss out of the line of fire was impossible to explain away as amateur luck. How was he supposed to spin this? Admit he spotted the scope glint? Claim he saw the bullet in mid-air?

Looks like last night's nightmare wasn't random—it was a premonition.

"Yi-an."

"Yes... Director Kang...?"

"Are you hurt?"

Il-hyun closed the distance and reached out. When Jakyeong flinched backward, Il-hyun caught his forearm in an unyielding grip, pulling him in close. He raised his free hand, his thumb brushing lightly across Jakyeong's cheek before showing him the fingertip. A faint streak of crimson stained the skin—a stray shard of flying glass had grazed his cheekbone.

Il-hyun’s face darkened, looking far more lethal than when he had ordered the glass contractor buried alive.

"Tch. Such a pretty face, ruined with a scratch."

Jakyeong blinked. Pretty face? Who talks like that, an eighty-year-old grandfather?

He stared in disgust, but Il-hyun looked genuinely moved.

"Thank you."

"..."

"It seems I owe you my life."

Jakyeong scrambled to weave an alibi. "No, please... It was pure luck. Ever since I was little, I've had this paranoid habit of constantly scanning my surroundings in case someone jumped me."

"Ah... so that kind of trauma actually has its uses."

"Yes..."

"For a second there, I thought you had the eyesight of a hawk."

"Haha... of course not."

"Or perhaps you turn into Superman the moment you take those glasses off?"

What the hell is that supposed to mean? Is he mocking me or complimenting me?

"Just a joke."

"Haha."

"Don't force the laugh."

"..."

Il-hyun patted Jakyeong’s shoulder reassuringly before signaling a maid to fetch an antiseptic ointment and fresh bandages. He then walked over to the ruined oil painting, letting out a string of creative curses. He mentioned it had cost a fortune at a private auction, swearing that once the perpetrator was caught, he’d bill them for the glass, the canvas, and the bullet holes.

How many assassination attempts do you have to survive to treat a sniper ambush like a minor inconvenience?

Jakyeong’s mind was spinning. The trajectory of those rounds hadn't been aimed at Il-hyun—they had been locked dead-center onto the spot where Jakyeong had been standing. Putting two consecutive rounds through the exact same coordinate wasn't an accident.

Someone was trying to kill me. Who? And why?

Il-hyun returned with the ointment and bandages in hand. Seeing him approach, Jakyeong quickly held out his palm. You're not seriously going to play nurse in front of the entire household, are you?

"Please, give it to me... I can apply it myself."

"You're the prince who saved my life," Il-hyun smiled sweetly. "The least I can do is dress the wound personally."

He crooked his finger in that familiar, condescending beckon. Does he really think he's calling a stray mutt?

Swallowing his pride, Jakyeong stepped forward. Il-hyun squeezed a dollop of cream onto his fingertip and gently smoothed it over the cut on Jakyeong’s cheek. He maintained steady, unbroken eye contact the entire time, forcing Jakyeong to avert his gaze in awkward misery.

Behind them, the staff was already sweeping up the broken glass. To Jakyeong's surprise, neither the housekeeper nor the maids seemed particularly shaken.

A sharp sting on his cheek made Jakyeong wince. Instantly, Il-hyun leaned in and blew a soft, cool breath—whoo—over the wound.

The intimate gesture sent an involuntary shiver down Jakyeong's spine, prompting him to take a sharp step back.

Il-hyun tilted his head, his eyes dancing with amusement as he carefully smoothed a sterile bandage over the cut.

Unable to bear the scrutiny, Jakyeong snapped his head away. "Thank you."

Il-hyun handed over the tube of ointment. "Take this. Apply it again later."

"Understood..."

"If it scars, feel free to send me the plastic surgery bill."

"Right..."

"And if you're traumatized, I'll compensate you for psychological distress."

"Right..."

"If you're too terrified to sleep alone, my master bedroom is open to you tonight. You have my permission."

Shut the fuck up, you absolute hound.

Even knowing it was a teasing jab, Jakyeong couldn't completely steady his breathing. The memory of that rock-hard ridge pressing against his rear during the tackle was still uncomfortably fresh. He glanced down involuntarily—sure enough, the prominent bulge beneath Il-hyun's tailored slacks was unmistakable.

Jakyeong stood speechless. Are you out of your mind? How does a man get turned on during a firefight?!

Il-hyun let out a smooth, radiant chuckle.

"Stay inside the estate today," he said, the playful mockery in his voice hardening into cold, absolute authority. "It seems our shooter was aiming for you, Yi-an."

So you noticed it too.

Without pressing the matter further, Il-hyun turned and strode out toward the courtyard with Park Tae-soo.

The housekeeper hurried over, checking Jakyeong for any other injuries with motherly concern. Jakyeong nodded reassuringly, looking down at the tube of ointment clutched in his hand. For some infuriating reason, the spot on his cheek where Il-hyun’s fingers had lingered still felt like it was burning.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • Dream Superstition (꿈은 반대): A classic Korean folk belief that dreams manifest in reverse (e.g., dreaming of death, gore, or getting mutilated foretells good fortune, while peaceful dreams portend bad luck). Jakyeong uses this to cope with his gruesome nightmare about Il-hyun.

  • Eyesight Scale / 5.0 (시력이 5.0): In South Korea, visual acuity is measured on a decimal scale where 1.0 to 1.5 is standard 20/20 vision, and 2.0 is exceptional. Saying someone has "5.0 vision" is an exaggeration akin to saying they have superhuman telescope eyes.
